analysis.title: International Market Intelligence Morning Briefing (October 26, 2026)
key_insights: JPM Market Intelligence is tentative into a busy week of central bank meetings (Fed, ECB, BOJ, all expected on hold with hawkish risk after the recent rates rally) and Mag7 and Korea memory earnings. Lula won a record fourth term in Brazil, and equities there are expected to be under pressure as fiscal consolidation is priced lower.

Global equities have been driven by two narratives: tech weakness and risk-off. Tech concern centers on financing, with capital the new AI bottleneck. Risk-off shows up as rotation into defensives and rates regaining safe-haven properties.

Drew stays tactically bullish on US equities on strong economic growth and positive earnings. In Europe, strong earnings (SXXP Q3 EPS growth 21.9% YoY) and stretched relative positioning vs the US should have driven broadening, but politics and spread pressure dominated. Moody's decision to maintain the French rating should support OATs today.

After 10 days marketing in APAC, clients are notably more bearish than in the US but perhaps less so than in Europe. APAC clients have outperformed global peers and are up double digits on the year, so many lack incentive to re-engage until a clear trend emerges.

US consumer remains robust. The top 4 income quintiles hold 6% to 27% more inflation-adjusted cash than at YE2019, nearly $8T nominal. Retail sales run $723bn per month YTD2026 vs $505bn in 2019. Credit card delinquencies are normalizing to pre-COVID trends, not deteriorating. JPM sees no evidence for an imminent consumer crack.

Consumer sub-sector views from clients: airlines, cruise and hotels have robust demand. Autos and homebuilders are rate-sensitive, and parts and suppliers may be better expressions. Retailers face freight costs flagged at 30-40% of total cost, with rates more than tripled YTD, plus LULU and NKE issues. Restaurants see trade-down within quick service as negative. Staples are most at risk of margin compression and likely a source of funds.

Corporate health is solid. SPX is near all-time highs ex post-recession periods, with record margins. HY default rates are 2.7% vs a 3.2% long-term average, after about 20% of HY market cap was upgraded to IG post-COVID.

AI infrastructure credit: markets are becoming more discriminating but there is no sign of a broader funding crisis. Hyperscalers are well positioned, while leveraged GPU and data center developers face tighter financing. AI infrastructure has absorbed more than $500B of debt YTD, and hyperscaler all-in funding costs are up about 120bps.

AI-related CDS spreads have widened on technical selling and bank hedging of data center lending exposure, not on deteriorating fundamentals. CDS now trades above comparable cash bonds, which JPM sees as an opportunity for bond investors willing to sell protection. CRWV is highlighted because it also has converts outstanding and CDS at a slightly positive basis.

US IG TMT credit: MSFT, GOOGL and AMZN spreads have held up, while externally financed names, especially ORCL, underperformed. ORCL and SpaceX widened on reports of off-balance-sheet financing. JPM credit expects growing debt supply may pressure spreads into 2027. Nvidia is a key transmission channel for financial stress given its ties to GPU customers including CRWV.

US HY TMT credit: CRWV has a financing challenge, not a solvency one. JPM's Tom Egan projects CRWV last-12-month EBITDA rising from about $4.4B in June 2026 to $7.3B by YE and nearly $20B by YE27, backed by about $130B of contracted revenue. Hyperscaler customers and vendors have incentive to support its financing.

France is viewed as an idiosyncratic story, not Sovereign Crisis 2.0. France has a roughly 3% primary deficit and debt/GDP near 120%, but a 180% threshold is 10-15 years away. Italy could stabilize debt with about 50bp of spending cuts vs more than 300bp for France. ECB backstops (TPI, OMT) limit disorderly widening, though activation is conditional.

OATs discount debt/GDP above 150% and an implied deficit above 8%, vs 120% and about 5% actual. About 60% of French debt is held by non-residents and HF crowding in carry proxies worsened the move. JPM calls for no material reversal until the 2Q27 elections but sees room for relief into year-end around the budget discussion.

EU banks: the tape echoes the 2011-12 sovereign crisis, but JPM sees earnings trends unchanged and says dips of more than 15% vs the index should be bought. The backdrop favors call ratio spreads and call spreads. French equities (exporters and domestics) are both shorted, making France a funder at country level.

Midterms: AI regulation at the federal level is unlikely because Trump would veto and Democrats cannot reach a two-thirds override. If Democrats take the House they could defund Middle East military efforts. Tariff policy is unlikely to change. Longer-dated bonds could get a bid if Democrats halt deficit spending. Single-sector views are not affected.

Treasuries: before the Oct 22 rally the view was 5.50% was more likely than 5.00% for the 10-year yield. Markets price a hike in Dec 2026 and two in FY27, and clients see upside risk to that on balance sheet strength, growth and inflation. Downside risk is a near-term end to the US/Iran conflict and normalization of oil, refined product and shipping costs, held with low conviction.

Client AI/tech pushback: semis revenue from supply-chain-driven price spikes is unsustainable in a DCF, neocloud turmoil may spread to the whole group with bankruptcy risk, and software is unlikely to be a funding source. Security and infrastructure software are consensus longs. Buy trigger is a positioning flush, hyperscaler capex confirmation, semis earnings, tighter credit and seasonality, pointing to early November.

Breadth is poor. Since the July 28 lows the SPX is +4.8% through Oct 22, but 69% of stocks lag the index and over half of the index has a negative return. This makes single-stock picks hedged with a sector ETF hard. An everything rally is possible short term but not longer term, with Tech dominance expected once markets stabilize.

Only about 65% of SPX companies mentioned AI operational improvement in 26Q2 earnings and under 5% quantified it. JPM wonders whether AI quantification becomes a management quality metric with a valuation discount for those who cannot quantify.

Cyclicals: clients focus on financials (GSIBs and credit cards). Aero/defense has a negative outlook on Blue Wave risk to military funding, though a lame-duck defense bill could surprise to the upside. Macro and the bullish yield-curve shift support cyclicals. To fund Tech longs, clients suggest consumer, healthcare, smid caps and Europe.

Other assets: Dollar seen range-bound and probably at a local high. Gold interesting after the decline but still trades inversely to the Dollar. No one viewed credit as superior to equities. Copper bull case agreed, tied to a China growth reboot. Silver viewed as part of the AI trade.

JPM remains tactically bullish on global equities with a regional preference for US and Asia (Japan, South Korea, Taiwan) over Europe. Longs: AI infrastructure (inference, semi cap), less-levered hyperscalers, AI-vulnerable application software, EU and JA banks, EU industrials, JA machinery, GE infra, EU miners, EU pharma and UKX. Shorts: AI-vulnerable ex-software, short-cycle data center capex, EU insurance, autos, chemicals, Asian consumer electronics, medtech and MDAX.
Option hedges: keep MCX < UKX until clarity emerges, and short France vs EU domestics on politics and dislocation.

EM: bullish after recovering over 9% of the drawdown since end-July. Trades: tactically long China Star 50 vs KWEB, tactically long Korea vs South East Asia, tactically long Taiwan as a less volatile AI exposure than Korea. Hedges: long Brazil (EWZ) on potential structural policy shift, and EM (EEM) for broadening exposure.

Positioning: HFs are -3.3% MTD globally (from -2.1% last week) vs SPX +0.2% MTD, driven by alpha. Eq L/S 20d alpha is the worst since Feb '21. HF selling on JPM's book was moderate. CTAs sold US equity exposure every day since 10/13, led by Nasdaq. Retail remained a net buyer but at the slowest pace in a year, and ETFs bought led by Tech.

Sector flows: combined ETF, retail and HF 60d flows into Info Tech are near record highs (+3z). Flows into Utilities, Real Estate and Materials are at or near extreme lows. Healthcare is the defensive exception.

Stabilization signals: crowding returns are low on a 60d basis, multi-strat de-grossing has slowed, quants are re-grossing and ETFs are buying the dip. Risks: Eq L/S alpha is still deteriorating, CTAs are neutral so could sell further (US exposure about 45th percentile), and retail demand is soft. Positioning has not fully cleared.

vol_and_positioning: Hedge funds are -3.3% MTD globally (from -2.1% last week), YTD +4.7% (from +6%), vs SPX +0.2% MTD and ACWI -1.0%.

Eq L/S 20d alpha (-2.9%) is the worst since Feb '21. Multi-strat alpha is the worst since Aug '24. 60d crowding returns (-4.1%) are back to July '24 levels, an episode that worsened before it rebounded.
HF net flows were only -0.9z (gross -0.6z). Multi-strat 5d de-grossing slowed to -0.9% from -3.3% a week ago. Quants kept adding gross (80th percentile).

CTAs were the most consistent sellers, with US equity exposure down every day since 10/13, led by Nasdaq. CTA US exposure is only about 45th percentile LT, so more selling is possible if markets do not rebound.
Retail stayed net buyer at the slowest pace in a year (5th percentile on 20d). ETFs were buyers, led by Tech.

Combined ETF, retail and HF 60d relative flows into Info Tech are near record highs (+3z vs +3.4z peak in late Sep). Utilities 60d -2.5z (lowest since Jan '24), Real Estate 20d -4.9z, Materials 60d -2.7z. Healthcare 20d +2.8z, HF-led.
US TPM is at the 28th percentile, Europe the 8th, China/HK at -2z.
Eq L/S net leverage is at 12m and 3yr lows, but gross leverage is still above average (77th percentile 12m, 95th 5yr) despite falling 4.4% WoW.
AI Core Revenue and Semis positioning fell to the 94th percentile LT from 99th.
French equities exporters and domestics are both shorted, making France a funder at country level. HF crowding in carry proxies worsened the OAT move.
geopolitical: Lula won a record fourth term in Brazil, a surprise outcome, with fiscal consolidation priced lower.
French fiscal and political stress is pressuring OATs and spreads. Moody's decision to maintain the French rating should support OATs. Elections are due in 2Q27.
US/Iran conflict: a near-term end could normalize oil, refined product, petrochemical and shipping and insurance rates, a low-conviction downside risk to rate-hike pricing.
US midterms: tariff policy unlikely to change, AI regulation at federal level unlikely, and a Democratic House could defund Middle East military efforts.
China Central Committee plenum kicks off in Beijing on 10/26.
US Secretary of State hosts a two-day G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting from 10/30.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers are fundamentally well positioned, capital remains available, the HY compute index is +372bps YTD, and CRWV has about $130b of contracted revenue and access to SPV and customer-backed financing.
tension_points.bear_case: Terms are tightening, borrowing costs are up about 120bps, growing debt supply may pressure spreads into 2027, and leveraged GPU and data center developers face rising financing constraints with Nvidia-linked concentration risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A move from selective tightening to a broad funding crisis, or failure of leveraged GPU developers to deliver contracted compute capacity on schedule.

tension_points.bull_case: France is idiosyncratic. Debt/GDP of 180% is 10-15 years away, ECB backstops exist, OATs price debt/GDP above 150% and a deficit above 8%, and relief is possible into year-end around the budget.
tension_points.bear_case: France has a ~3% primary deficit, debt/GDP near 120% and below-potential growth. Tape behavior echoes the 2011-12 sovereign crisis with EGB spreads wider and EU banks lower.
tension_points.what_invalidates: ECB backstop activation being required, which JPM says is conditional, or the 2Q27 elections shifting fiscal policy.

tension_points.bull_case: Fundamentals remain positive, security and infrastructure software are consensus longs, and tech flows are near record highs with positioning cleared in part.
tension_points.bear_case: Semis revenue driven by supply-chain price spikes is unsustainable in a DCF, neocloud turmoil may spread, and positioning has not fully cleared.
tension_points.what_invalidates: JPM's buy trigger is a positioning flush, hyperscaler capex confirmation, semis earnings, tighter credit and positive seasonality, pointing to early November.
